keyChanges.title: Reuters: Tesla pressured EU regulators to seal FSD safety data before October bloc-wide vote
keyChanges.description: A Reuters investigation published August 6, 2026, based on emails obtained via Dutch public-records request, reveals that Tesla conditioned its cooperation with the Netherlands' RDW type-approval process on guarantees that safety evaluation documents would never be released publicly. The emails show Tesla began pressing RDW to keep FSD review documentation permanently sealed as early as late 2024. The Dutch regulator honored the demand: it will not disclose how it evaluated the technology, what test protocols were used, or what performance thresholds were required, despite RDW's subsequent push for EU-wide recognition of that same sealed approval. Separately, regulators in six EU countries including Germany, Norway, and Denmark told Reuters they cannot release FSD testing or performance data either, citing Tesla's trade-secret claims. A prior Reuters investigation in May 2026 found that Tesla's own published FSD safety statistics are significantly inflated — the company counted only severe crashes for its own fleet while using broader figures for overall crash rates, and assumed 100% fleet replacement by FSD-equipped Teslas to inflate lives-saved projections. The October 6 TCMV vote would authorize a type approval for all 27 EU member states based on a safety case that no member of the European public — and no non-approving regulator — has been permitted to see. The European Transport Safety Council (ETSC), which wrote to EU transport ministers on June 30, 2026 following a fatal Texas FSD crash, has urged ministers to withhold recognition until safety data is independently verified publicly.

positive_signals: RDW states it ran its own closed-track and public-road testing and did not rely solely on Tesla's inflated statistics
October 6 TCMV vote is now scheduled — a formal path to EU-wide recognition exists
negative_signals: Tesla emails show the company conditioned RDW cooperation on permanent confidentiality guarantees since late 2024
Six EU regulators (Germany, Norway, Denmark, and others) cannot release FSD testing data due to Tesla trade-secret claims
October 6 TCMV vote would ratify a safety case with no public transparency — no independent verification published
Reuters May 2026 investigation found Tesla's published FSD safety statistics are materially inflated (cherry-picked crash metrics, 100% fleet-replacement assumption)
RDW's own stated confidence already retreated from 'safer than other ADAS' (April) to 'at least as safe' (June)
ETSC urging EU ministers to block recognition until safety data is verified — adds political friction ahead of October vote
France and Sweden are known TCMV opponents; data-secrecy revelations increase the chance other states join opposition

keyChanges.title: TCMV October 6 EU-wide FSD vote confirmed via German Ministry email; outcome far from certain
keyChanges.description: An official email from Germany's Federal Ministry of Transport, shared publicly around late July 2026, confirmed that the Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) has a session scheduled for October 6, 2026, at which a vote on EU-wide approval of FSD (Supervised) is planned. If the vote achieves a qualified majority — at least 15 of 27 member states representing at least 65% of EU population — the European Commission would issue an implementing act authorizing the Dutch RDW approval to extend across all member states simultaneously. However, the outcome is highly uncertain: France's Transport Minister publicly rejected current FSD Supervised in late July, Sweden's transport authority has raised formal speed-offset objections to the TCMV, and the August 6 Reuters investigation into sealed safety data adds further political risk. Germany's KBA, which received a dedicated Tesla vehicle for independent evaluation in July 2026, has not reached a position. The ETSC has formally urged EU transport ministers to block recognition without public safety verification. A December vote or 2027 slip is explicitly flagged by multiple trackers if October fails. No new national approvals were granted in the July 23 - August 6 window; total consumer markets remain 6 (US + NL/LT/EE/DK/BE).

positive_signals: October 6 TCMV vote date now confirmed from official German Federal Ministry of Transport communication — formal EU-wide approval pathway is live
If passed, a single implementing act would unlock FSD across all 27 EU member states simultaneously
Germany is actively reviewing (test vehicle received July 2026) rather than flatly opposing
Finland's Traficom signaling possible pre-October national approval — could add a 7th consumer market
negative_signals: France officially rejected current FSD Supervised configuration (speeding + driver monitoring gaps) — a large-population no vote risk
Sweden raised formal TCMV objections over speed offset; Finland, Norway, Denmark also have outstanding speed/icy-road questions
Reuters data-secrecy revelations raise political barrier for ministers who have not yet seen safety evidence
Qualified majority threshold (15 states + 65% population) is high — France alone accounts for ~15% EU population
October slot could slip to December or 2027 if any procedural objection delays the TCMV agenda
Major markets (Germany, France, Italy, Spain, UK) all still closed; 5 small-country footprint unchanged

keyChanges.title: Finland Traficom opens formal FSD review, signals possible approval before October EU vote
keyChanges.description: Finland's Transport and Communications Agency Traficom publicly stated it is assessing Tesla FSD (Supervised) for national type-approval recognition and is engaging directly with Tesla and other EU member state authorities. Traficom signaled it is prepared to move faster than the October 6 TCMV bloc-wide decision, provided Tesla resolves a handful of outstanding technical questions specific to Finnish operating conditions: (1) driver retake-of-control speed — how quickly drivers can assume control when FSD exits; (2) overtaking behavior in low-visibility conditions typical on Finnish rural roads; (3) the speed-offset feature that allows FSD to exceed posted limits to match traffic flow — the same issue Sweden and Norway have raised at TCMV level. If Traficom grants national recognition before October 6, Finland would become the 7th consumer market globally (6th in EU) for FSD Supervised. However, Traficom has not issued approval and all three technical questions remain open. Given Sweden's parallel TCMV objection on the same speed-offset issue, it is not clear Tesla has resolved the underlying regulatory concern that is also blocking the EU-wide vote.

positive_signals: Traficom officially opened formal review and is engaging with Tesla — Finland is on an active approval track, not a wait-and-see posture
Possibility of a 7th consumer market (6th EU) before October if Tesla answers technical questions
Traficom framed this as a technical gap-closing exercise, not a political rejection
Finland would add a Nordic market, expanding EU footprint beyond current Baltic/Benelux cluster
negative_signals: No approval granted yet — all three technical questions (retake speed, overtaking, speed offset) still open
Speed-offset concern mirrors Sweden's formal TCMV objection — Tesla has not publicly resolved this regulatory sticking point
Finland is a relatively small market (~5.5M population); approval here does not meaningfully advance the October EU vote math
Traficom has not committed to a timeline; 'ahead of October' is aspirational, not a deadline

metricUpdate.note: No new country approvals granted July 23 - August 6. Total consumer markets remain 6: US + NL/LT/EE/DK/BE. Finland under Traficom review (potential 7th, not yet approved). Germany KBA review ongoing, not approved.

categoryUpdate.latestStatus: FSD consumer markets unchanged at 6 (US + 5 small EU). October 6 TCMV EU-wide vote now officially scheduled but faces France opposition and data-secrecy political headwinds following Reuters investigation. Finland potentially becoming 7th market pre-October if speed-offset questions resolved.
